title: Generation Time (Doubling Time)

references.label: General microbiology/quantitative methods references (ASM, FDA BAM)

expression: g = t / n, where n = log10(N/N0) / log10(2)
explanation: During exponential growth, the number of generations (n) that occurred over a time interval (t) is found from the starting and ending population sizes; dividing the elapsed time by the number of generations gives the generation time (g) — the average time for the population to double once. This is only valid for the portion of a growth curve that is truly in exponential (log) phase; applying it across lag or stationary phase data will give a meaningless result.

variables.meaning: Elapsed time between the two measurements, in the same time units as g
Number of generations (doublings) that occurred over that interval
Population size (or CFU/mL, or OD) at the end of the interval
Population size (or CFU/mL, or OD) at the start of the interval

workedExample.scenario: A culture grows from 1×10^3 CFU/mL to 8×10^3 CFU/mL over 90 minutes, entirely within exponential phase.

commonMistakes: Applying the formula to data that spans lag or stationary phase rather than pure exponential-phase growth.
Mixing units for N (e.g. CFU/mL for N0 and OD for N) — both measurements in the ratio must be in the same units.
Assuming a generation time calculated under one set of conditions (temperature, medium) applies under different conditions.
